document.title: A/S Raphel Discusses Afghanistan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Assistant Secretary Robin Raphel meets Pakistani, Kabul government and Taliban officials. Gen. Karamat calls the Taliban "a millstone around our necks" and Bhutto claims only non-lethal aid. Masoud says Pakistan is as much to blame as the Soviets. The Taliban say "If the U.N. fails, then we have failed."

events.description: Raphel visited Afghanistan April 19-20, meeting Kabul government leaders and Taliban leaders including Muttaqi and five inner shura members, and the Russian aircrew in Kandahar.
Raphel met in Islamabad with PM Bhutto, COAS Karamat, Interior Minister Babar, FM Assef Ali, Foreign Secretary Shaikh and UN officials.
Recent Kandahar ulema majlis elevated Mullah Omar to 'Leader of the Faithful' and rejected negotiations.
Embassy Islamabad cable reporting on Raphel's Afghanistan discussions.
A/S Raphel visits Afghanistan (April 19-20) meeting Kabul government officials and Taliban leaders including five members of inner shura.
Raphel meets Pakistani officials in Islamabad: Bhutto, Karamat, Babar, Assef Ali, Shaikh, and UN officials.
Recent Kandahar ulema majlis rejects negotiations and elevates Mullah Omar to 'Leader of the Faithful'.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reporting Raphel's discussions on the Afghan peace process.
A/S Raphel held talks with Kabul government leaders Rabbani, Massoud, Lafraie; they criticized Pakistan and Taliban and agreed in principle to send a delegation to Pakistan.
A/S Raphel met Taliban leaders including Motaqi, urged release of Russian aircrew, and discussed arms embargo and peace process.
Raphel met the detained Russian aircrew for 15 minutes in the Kandahar governor's compound.
Taliban stopped allowing the Russian aircrew to be photographed.

key_claims: Pakistan's government recognized its Taliban support had backfired and sought to broaden its Afghan policy.
COAS Karamat called the Taliban 'a millstone around our necks'.
Bhutto claimed Pakistan provided only minimal non-lethal aid to the Taliban.
The Taliban held a Russian aircrew in Kandahar and refused release until 60,000 missing Afghans in the former USSR were accounted for.
Rabbani said Sayyaf may have been involved in terrorism but lacked funds now.
Massoud and Lafraie accused Pakistan of being as much to blame for destruction as the Soviets.
